# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Top picks**

| Need | Pick | Price in the results | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best overall | Bose Ultra Open Earbuds | $199 (down from $299) | Runner's World's top pick. It has clear sound, a secure clip fit, and physical buttons that are easy to use mid-run. It's only IPX4 with about 7 hours per charge. |
| Best bone conduction | Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 | $125 to $180, depending on retailer | It's IP55 with 12 hours of battery and physical controls. WIRED found it has more bass but less clarity than the Bose. |
| Best for long or wet runs | Shokz OpenDots 2 | $200 | WIRED's top open-earbud pick. It has 10 hours of battery (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating. |
| Best value for running | Nothing Ear (Open) | $99 at Amazon (MSRP $149) | SoundGuys' top open-ear pick and its running pick in the workout roundup. It has strong bass for the category and IP54. |
| Budget | Soundcore AeroFit 2 | $80 to $104 | It has a hook design, IP55, and 10 hours per charge (42 with the case). |
| Cheapest way to try the category | JLab Flex Open | About $40 to $50 | It has less bass and detail, but Runner's World calls it the lowest-risk way to test clip-ons. |

**How to choose**
- **Bose Ultra Open:** It aims sound at the ear canal, so there's less leakage. Runner's World found it a bit quiet in heavy city traffic, and it isn't ideal for heavy rain. Bose is reportedly releasing new open-ear earbuds within a month, so you may want to wait.
- **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2:** It leaves your ears the most open and is the sturdiest of the group. The neckband can interfere with long hair and winter hats, and some people find the cheekbone pressure bothersome.
- **Nothing Ear (Open):** The sound is good for the price, and it has multipoint connectivity and a customizable EQ.
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2:** It costs the least but still has a sweat-resistant, secure hook fit. Open-ear designs in general leak sound and give no isolation.

**Where to buy**
I couldn't verify direct retailer product pages from these results, so these links go to the pages that list current prices and retailer options. Prices vary by retailer and change often, so check at checkout.
- Bose Ultra Open, Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, OpenDots 2, JLab Flex Open: [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) and [WIRED's best open earbuds](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (Amazon, REI, Best Buy options): [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)
- Nothing Ear (Open) and Soundcore AeroFit 2 (Amazon): [SoundGuys open-ear guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- Soundcore AeroFit 2 at Soundcore's US store: [Dealectric link](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. It lists the price as $129.99, or about $104 with code AFSC20 (not valid on items already on sale), which is higher than SoundGuys' Amazon price of $79.99.

For a head-to-head between the Bose and the Shokz, see the [RTINGS comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946). RTINGS rates the Bose slightly better for most people, but the Shokz is tougher and works with piercings.

**My suggestion:** Get the Nothing Ear (Open) or Soundcore AeroFit 2 for the best value, the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 if you want maximum awareness and durability, or the Bose if sound quality matters most. Whichever you pick, keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.
